# Purpose and scope

This Process Characterization Plan (**PCP-003**) defines the Stage 1 (Process
Design) characterization of the **A-Mab production bioreactor (Step 3)**, the
fed-batch cell-culture operation that establishes the glycosylation,
charge-variant and initial size-variant and process-impurity profile of the
drug substance. The plan specifies the quality attributes in scope, the process
parameters and ranges to be studied, the experimental designs, the analytical
methods, and the acceptance and decision criteria by which each parameter will be
classified and a design space established.

**Scope.** The `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"`-L commercial-scale
production bioreactor, characterized on a qualified 2 L scale-down model (SDM).
Seed-train expansion (Steps 1–2) and harvest (Step 4) are addressed only where
they affect the production culture; their characterization is out of scope of
this plan. This plan governs execution only — the results are reported in the
paired **Process Characterization Report (PCR-003)**.

**Basis.** The unit-operation model, quality-attribute framework and risk
methodology follow the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]; the Stage 1 approach and
report structure follow PDA Technical Report 60 [@pdatr60] and the ISPE Good
Practice Guide [@ispegpg2023]; the Quality-by-Design framework follows ICH Q8,
Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11].

# Unit-operation description

The production bioreactor is a fed-batch mammalian cell culture operated at
`{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L working volume. It is the only
upstream operation that forms product-quality CQAs and therefore the only
upstream step used to define the upstream design space [@amab2009]; the seed
expansion and harvest steps affect titer and process consistency but not product
quality. Product quality established here — N-glycosylation (afucosylation, high
mannose, galactosylation), charge variants, aggregate, and the host-cell protein
(HCP) and DNA impurity load — is the input to the purification train
(@fig-flow-ptp).

![A-Mab drug-substance process flow (Steps 3–10); the production bioreactor (Step 3) forms the product-quality attributes characterized in this plan.](../outputs/figures/fig_process_flow.png){#fig-flow-ptp width=100%}

# Quality attributes in scope

The characterization targets the CQAs that are set or principally controlled by
the production bioreactor (@tbl-cqa-ptp). Criticality is assessed on the A-Mab
continuum using Tool #1 (Risk Score = Impact × Uncertainty); attributes rated
High (H) or Very High (VH) are treated as *Critical* [@amab2009; @ichq9].
Acceptance criteria are the drug-substance ranges carried from the CQA
assessment and are the pass/fail basis for the study responses.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
```

: CQAs in scope for the production-bioreactor characterization, with acceptance criteria and criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty). {#tbl-cqa-ptp}

The study responses measured for these CQAs are afucosylation, galactosylation,
high mannose and acidic charge variants (released assays), and aggregate (SEC);
the harvest HCP and DNA impurity load is followed as a performance response since
it is cleared downstream.

# Parameters and ranges to be characterized

Nine process parameters are in scope (@tbl-param-ptp). Each is studied across the
range shown ("Range studied"), which becomes the basis for the proven acceptable
range (PAR); the normal operating range (NOR) is the tighter range at which the
parameter will be controlled in routine manufacturing. The study type
(multivariate vs univariate) is assigned by the risk-ranking-and-filtering screen
of the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment (**RA-001**): parameters with
a credible main-effect and interaction risk to CQAs are studied multivariately;
parameters expected to affect only performance are studied univariately or held
at their set-point [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
```

: Production-bioreactor process parameters, set-points, characterization ranges and study type. Classification is an output of the study and is reported in PCR-003. {#tbl-param-ptp}

Culture pH, temperature, dissolved CO₂, osmolality and culture duration are
carried into the multivariate design as the parameters with the greatest
prior-knowledge risk to the glycan and charge-variant CQAs. Dissolved oxygen,
initial viable cell concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume are assessed for
their effect on process performance (peak viable cell density, titer, viability);
basal medium concentration is studied over a wide range as a general parameter.

# Study design

Characterization uses a sequential design-of-experiments (DoE) strategy executed
on the qualified 2 L SDM under **SOP-1002**, with the SDM qualified against
at-scale reference data under **SOP-1001**:

1. **Screening design** — a resolution-V two-level fractional factorial in the
   five multivariate factors (culture pH, temperature, dissolved CO₂, osmolality
   and culture duration) with centre points, **`{python} n_scr` runs total**,
   to identify the parameters and interactions with significant effects on the
   glycan, charge-variant and aggregate responses.
2. **Response-surface design** — a face-centred central-composite design in the
   dominant factors carried forward from screening (culture pH, temperature,
   culture duration and dissolved CO₂), **`{python} n_rsm` runs total**, to
   quantify main effects, two-factor interactions and curvature and to define the
   multivariate design space.
3. **Univariate assessment** — initial viable cell concentration is evaluated one
   factor at a time for its effect on process performance.

All runs are executed on the SDM at the commercial working volume equivalent and
harvested on the nominal culture-duration criterion. Responses are measured by
the validated methods in @tbl-sop: released N-glycan map (afucosylation, high
mannose, galactosylation) under **AMV-3010**, charge variants (acidic variants)
under **AMV-3013**, aggregate (SEC) under **AMV-3011**, and the harvest HCP and
residual-DNA load under **AMV-3012** and **AMV-3014**.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The study is acceptable when the fitted response-surface models are adequate
(coefficient of determination and residual diagnostics per **SOP-1002**) and the
design space satisfies every in-scope CQA simultaneously at the set-point and
across the NOR. Each parameter is then classified per the A-Mab continuum
[@amab2009], consistent with the rule applied in the post-characterization risk
assessment:

- A parameter whose variability significantly impacts a CQA is a **critical
  process parameter (CPP)**; where the impact is reliably controlled within the
  design space (low risk of leaving it) the parameter is a **well-controlled CPP
  (WC-CPP)**.
- A parameter that does not significantly impact a CQA but affects process
  performance or consistency is a **key process parameter (KPP)**; otherwise it is
  a **general process parameter (GPP)**.
- Consistent with the FMEA convention, a parameter that affects a CQA with
  Severity ≥ 8, or that carries an initial risk priority number > 72, is
  designated a CPP before mitigation by the control strategy.

The design space, parameter classification and the proven acceptable ranges
established here provide the justification for the Stage 2 (PPQ) operating ranges
and feed the overall control strategy.
